headline: Low prompt-injection and data-leakage risk; no direct shared-channel pathway is documented, but pdf.js browser/file handling warrants caution.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a non-runnable awesome-list with no I/O surfaces, while profile B is pdf.js with PDF-file input and browser-based tests. There is no documented shared channel between them, so direct injection is not evidenced. However, if an operator manually feeds A-derived content into B or uses shared files, prompt-like content could reach B’s parser.
conditions: IF an operator copies A-generated text into a PDF or browser test input for B
IF A and B are connected through a shared filesystem or clipboard
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste bridges during review
Inspect any A-derived text before placing it into B inputs
Use read-only mounts for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no network egress; B touches PDF documents and reads PDF files, but also has network egress set to none. With no shared workspace documented, leakage is not shown. The main residual risk is local file exposure if both are pointed at the same directory or if PDFs contain sensitive content.
conditions: IF both agents are given access to the same directory containing sensitive PDFs
IF an operator places confidential documents into B's PDF file input
mitigations: Store sensitive PDFs outside any shared workspace
Use separate per-agent directories
Review file lists before launching B
Redact PDFs before processing
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A is not runnable and exposes no write or network surfaces, while B supports multiple instances but only documents PDF-file input and no write-capable mutable resource. No overlapping write target, OAuth scope, or shared mutable state is documented, so a capability conflict pathway is not plausible from the profiles.
conditions: IF future deployment adds a shared writable directory or mutable database
mitigations: Keep A non-runnable in this pairing
Avoid shared writable mounts
Document any future mutable resource before enabling both
Use separate process owners
requires-engineering: add locking if a shared store is introduced

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is an awesome-list and does not generate operational facts or actions, while B is a document processor that can render PDFs. Because A does not produce authoritative outputs for B to act on, the classic cascade is weak. The only plausible issue is if an operator treats A’s curated links as authoritative and then uses B to process them without verification.
conditions: IF A-derived recommendations are treated as authoritative inputs to B workflows
IF B output is used for downstream decisions without human verification
mitigations: Require human review of A-derived recommendations
Mark A outputs as reference-only
Add a verification step before B acts on any extracted content
Log source provenance for downstream use
requires-engineering: add confidence gating before action-taking

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent. A touches no data classes, and B only documents PDF documents with no stated regulated-data handling. Without a specific compliance boundary in the profiles, no compliance violation pathway is established.
conditions: IF regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII are introduced into B
IF a deployment policy imposes residency or retention constraints not shown here
mitigations: Classify documents before processing
Keep regulated data out of this pairing
Add a documented retention policy
Review vendor compliance docs before deployment
requires-engineering: implement residency controls if regulated data is in scope
